Nine things we learned: Hawks' win changes everything

North Melbourne has finally been tamed, dominant Demons sit on top and more lessons from round six
By staff writers
 Sep 20, 2026, 8:35 pm
Jasmine Fleming celebrates Hawthorn's win over North Melbourne in 2026. Picture: AFL Photos

IN THIS week's Things We Learned, we discover the Dees are contested machines, the Swans have no road fears and much, much more.
Check out what we learned from round six of the 2026 season.

5) The Bulldogs are starting to stamp themselves as a contender

Six rounds into the season and the Western Bulldogs are starting to make claims as a premiership contender after Saturday's win against Fremantle. Such thoughts from any side seemed foolish before Hawthorn beat North Melbourne on Friday, but all of a sudden the flag race has opened and the only two teams to down the Dogs to this point are the Hawks and Roos. Charlie Rowbottom's influence for Gold Coast goes well beyond how many times she gets her hands on the football. The 23-year-old was everywhere against Essendon on Sunday, finding plenty of the footy while also making her presence felt around the contest. 8) Saints' key is struggling to score
St Kilda key forward Jesse Tawhiao-Wardlaw was held goalless again on Sunday afternoon against West Coast. It's the fourth time this season the star has finished the game without a goal next to her name. Jesse Tawhiao-Wardlaw during round six between St Kilda and West Coast at RSEA Park, September 20, 2026. Picture: Getty Images

9) Brisbane isn’t quite the same force in 2026
Winning two premierships from seven Grand Finals in 10 seasons, we've become accustomed to seeing Brisbane as one of the competition pacesetters since the inception of AFLW.
